messages:
ops-alert-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate on dedicated-us-east-1a. p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.3s at 2026-02-17T03:11:12Z. 3 customer escalations auto-created.

maria (support): got three customers on this already — two are paying Dedicated customers, one is a partner using private deployment. They report timeouts and UI stalls. Sharing customer IDs via DMs.

aisha (oncall-sre): coming in. can someone post the p95/p99 numbers and which hosts are impacted? any recent infra changes in that region? @kevin

kevin (infra): grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/serve?orgId=1&var-cluster=dedicated-us-east-1a — p95 ~600ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~420ms -> 2.3s starting at 03:10 UTC. A rollout finished ~02:50 UTC: host kernel 6.6.11 -> 6.7.0 on the node pool, and GPU driver bumped from 532.x -> 535.86 as part of CUDA 12.2 image. I also see a spike in NVMe avg latency on /dev/nvme0n1 on a subset of machines.

samir (eng-runtime): interesting. did the rollout include any runtime change? model binaries unchanged. We recently flipped a small kv-cache async write optimization but that was pushed last week and only enabled behind a feature flag. Not enabled in dedicated default.

kevin (infra): attaching iostat and nvme-cli outputs from host rde-ue1-03 (one of the bad nodes):

```
Device            tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    kB_read    kB_wrtn
nvme0n1         5400      120000       98000     4320000    3520000
nvme0n1 avgqu-sz  0.25   await  8.12  svctm  0.24
# nvme-cli log:  tail latency histogram shows 99th bucket 2.1s
```

kevin (infra): the weird bit is that throughput isn't saturated — it's IO tail latency. kernel upgrade + new driver + firmware version mismatch could be upsetting MSI-X/interrupt handling and causing scattered high latencies under certain qdepth patterns.

aisha (oncall-sre): ok repro plan: 1) isolate canary node, 2) synthetic steady-state load mimicking prefix-heavy chat requests (open loop ~50 concurrent streams), 3) run nvme qdepth sweep and measure p99. @samir can you run runtime profiler so we can correlate GPU stalls vs NVMe stalls?

samir (eng-runtime): on it. starting profiler on canary. will also capture tensor/core stalls and kernel scheduling gaps.

maria (support): I sent a polite update to impacted customers: "we're investigating a p99 latency regression affecting some dedicated clusters; engineering is running targeted tests and will share mitigations shortly." Template used: "We understand the impact — investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline."

kevin (infra): started rollback of driver on canary host to 532.x to match the rest of fleet. command I used:

```
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 && sudo apt remove --purge nvidia-driver-535 -y
sudo apt install nvidia-driver-532 -y
sudo reboot
```

kevin (infra): note: need to coordinate with CUDA image team if any runtime libs require symbol changes.

infra-bot: deployment note: host rde-ue1-03 cordoned, traffic moved off.

aisha (oncall-sre): great. samir, any correlation results yet?

samir (eng-runtime): profiler + perf shows long waits in kernel I/O wq handling; GPU kernel launch latency sometimes waiting on host page faults when nvme read latency spikes. correlation coefficient p99_io -> p99_token_latency ~0.86 on canary under synthetic load. When I replaced model access to use in-memory cached weights (bypass NVMe reads) p99 dropped back to ~480ms.

kevin (infra): after driver rollback on canary and a reboot, re-ran synthetic workload. p99 down to 510ms, p95 stable ~580ms — so rollback looks promising as mitigation.

aisha (oncall-sre): temporary mitigation: 1) halt kernel/driver rollout, 2) schedule controlled rollback to previous driver on affected node pool, 3) enable routing policy to favor nodes with older driver for customer traffic until we confirm vendor fix.

devex: for Dedicated customers hitting this we can also offer temporary traffic-shift to dedicated-backup / smaller quantized model variant via API route override. command to force fallback route:

```
redwoodctl routes set --cluster dedicated-us-east-1a --route /v1/generate --fallback-model rwd-small-q8
```

maria (support): sending updated customer note with ETA: "we have a mitigation path — rolling back driver on impacted nodes; expected reduction in p99 within 30 minutes for affected clusters; full fleet rollback scheduled pending sign-off."

kevin (infra): creating infra change: CHG-2026-0912 — plan: rollback driver to 532.x for node pool eu1-dedicated-pool-3, monitor 1h, then roll other pools progressively. Will coordinate with CUDA image team and oncall.

samir (eng-runtime): long term root causes to investigate: 1) driver 535.x + kernel 6.7 interaction with NVMe IRQ handling, 2) GPU firmware vs driver handshake under concurrent small reads, 3) our KV-cache write pattern may be exacerbating host I/O bursts — add rate limiting. I'll draft tests and bisect with vendor.

aisha (oncall-sre): current status: canary rollback successful, p99 back near baseline. ACTIONS:
- kevin (infra): rollback node-pool eu1-dedicated-pool-3 -> owner, ETA 45m
- samir (eng-runtime): run detailed bisect with 3 kernel/driver combinations and share perf artifacts -> owner, ETA EOD
- maria (support): follow-up messages to impacted customers with mitigation steps -> owner, ETA 15m
- devex: prepare route-fallback playbook and customer-facing instructions -> owner, ETA 1h

maria (support): filing CRO ticket and adding affected customer list.

aisha (oncall-sre): will keep this thread open until fleet stable for 2 hours post-rollback. if anything changes ping @aisha. thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

kevin (infra): ongoing: I'll post status updates to this thread during rollout.

infra-bot: CHG-2026-0912 created by kevin (infra) at 2026-02-17T04:02:10Z

kevin (infra): quick note — avoid kernel downgrade for now; vendor recommends driver rollback first. planning vendor engagement for a proper patch.

samir (eng-runtime): logging artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/p99-regressions/1729002222/ — perf profiles, nvme histograms, profiler captures.

aisha (oncall-sre): closing interim: canary looks stable. we'll reconvene if rollback in other pools does not behave. thread will remain for postmortem notes.

maria (support): thanks team — customers updated, CS will escalate if any new reports come in."
